name: Chains and sprockets
summary: Roller chain and toothed sprockets that pass power without slipping: bikes, motorbikes, go-karts and machines.
uses: Gearing a motor down to drive a pump or winch drum
Replacing a worn drive on a mower or cart
identify: Bike chain is everywhere; motorbikes, go-karts, garage door openers, conveyors and farm machines use heavier sizes like #35, #40 and #420, often stamped on the side plates. A sprocket must match the chain’s pitch and width.
test: Lay the chain flat and look for stiff links, rust and stretch: a worn chain lifts off the back of the sprocket. Sprocket teeth should be even, not hooked.

decay.note: Lasts if oiled; dry chain rusts stiff but often frees up with oil.
